text: Argh, lost another thought, man! Damn app, too many taps. But you know what? This is exactly why frictionless capture is crucial for us with ADHD brains. It's like a dam bursting - thoughts, ideas, they flow when we can free them fast. Zero-friction means zero-delay, and that matters because every second lost is a thought lost, a moment missed. Let's do better for our minds.

Okay, so here's the thing... saved tabs, tasks, ideas... it feels like a mountain, right? Yea, me too. And I've noticed something, just now... I keep saving stuff 'for later', then they pile up and become this heavy load, man. It's crazy how it clutters my mind and makes me avoid the whole system, even though it was supposed to help! Wait, actually... this isn't new. It's like a cycle. Dang, gotta break this cycle.

Okay, so basically I figured it out again, I need a bit of noise to get things done, but not too much. Gotta find that sweet spot like a cafe or some background tunes. 'Yo self, so I just realized something cool. When I start talking about stuff, even if it's just to myself, I feel like I get it way more than when I'm reading it. Man, this project's at like 70%, and I keep dropping it. It's just like school - do all the fun parts, then freeze up before final submission. Guess I've always got that pattern. Don't know how to break it yet, but I see it now.

'I just...realized. This ain't just about creating an app anymore. It's about relieving a burden, a weight I've carried for years. I mean, building something that could have helped me manage my thoughts when I was younger. You see, this app is about more than memory or organization, it's about freedom...freedom from the clutter in our heads, the constant struggle to remember everything. This project was born out of necessity, a need I experienced firsthand. It's like we're creating a tool that can externalize our minds, helping us not to drown in our own thoughts. That's why I'm building this app.'

Got this! So it turns out olive oil vs coconut oil are not just substitutes. Olive oil is rich in monounsaturated fats, great for heart health but sensitive to heat — use for salad dressings and low-heat cooking. Coconut oil, on the other hand, has a high smoke point and saturated fats making it ideal for stir-frys and deep frying. Gotta remember this because I keep using them interchangeably. Good to know!

Just read about ACT - Acceptance and Commitment Therapy. It's a psychological method helping people to accept their emotions & thoughts and commit to actions based on values instead of trying to avoid or suppress feelings. Really resonates with my struggle to manage emotional overload. This could be a powerful tool for me!
